title: agent instructions show
description: The rules e-designer gives an AI agent, merged from the three levels of AgentInstructions documents (built-in, machine, project; their merge is that schema's to say), from agent show; the Settings page reads the same answer over HTTP. Each rule names the level it came from, and the answer lists the levels read, so a person sees where a rule came from and which file to change.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/designer/app/v1: the form of e-designer's answers. An app's answers keep the family app (apiversion/v1/forms.yaml), apart from the files they describe.

kind.description: Always AgentInstructionsShow, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

ran.description: Where the answer came from; this contract fixes the app and the contract version, so an answer from anything else fails here.

app.description: Always designer, e-designer's product ID, since only e-designer gives this answer.

contract.description: Always v1, the contract version this schema belongs to.

data.description: The merged rules and the levels they were merged from.

rules.description: The rules the agent gets, in the order it reads them, after the merge. A rule a higher level removes is not listed, as the agent does not get it.

items.description: One merged rule and the level that gave it.

id.description: The rule's id, as the AgentInstructions documents name it.

text.description: What the agent is told: the text of the level that gave the rule.

origin.description: The level whose document gave this text, so a person knows which file to change to change the rule.

levels.description: Every level, in merge order from lowest to highest: built-in, machine, project. Each is listed whether or not it has a document, so a reader sees which files were read and which were missing.

prefixItems.description: The built-in level, shipped inside the app. It has no file, so it has no path, and it is always found.

found.description: Always true: the built-in rules are part of the app.

prefixItems.description: The machine level: the user's own document, for every project on this machine.

path.description: Where this level's document is read from on the machine the CLI ran on, absolute, so a person knows which file to open to change it. Given even when no file is there, as that is where one would be read from.

found.description: Whether a document was at path and read. False means the machine level added nothing.

prefixItems.description: The project level: the document kept with the design, for everyone who works on it.

path.description: Where this level's document is read from on the machine the CLI ran on, absolute, so a person knows which file to open to change it. Given even when no file is there, as that is where one would be read from.

found.description: Whether a document was at path and read. False means the project level added nothing.

level.description: A level of AgentInstructions documents: built-in (shipped with the app), machine (the user's own) or project (kept with the design).
